# Spec Vocabulary

Headers: `winui/ui/spec/Common.hpp`, `winui/ui/spec/Spec.hpp`, `winui/ui/spec/Control.hpp`, `winui/ui/spec/LayoutSpec.hpp`, `winui/ui/spec/ItemsModel.hpp`, `winui/ui/spec/Dynamic.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/spec/Common.hpp`.

## `ui::Style`

A named, composable bundle of layout defaults: the margin, the six sizes and the two alignments every spec carries. `.style = app_styles::Card` gives every card the same room, and works on every spec.

Composition is compile-time: `styles::Spaced | styles::Centered` is a constant expression, with the right-hand side winning wherever it sets a field. Unset fields (std::nullopt) pass through, so two partial styles combine. A field set on the spec itself wins over the style's.

Typography is not part of a style: a [ui::Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) takes `.role` (a step of the theme's type ramp) or `.text_style`, and a control with a foreground takes `.foreground`.

Example: 
```cpp
namespace app_styles
{
inline constexpr ui::Style Card = ui::styles::Spaced | ui::Style{.min_width = 200.0f};
}

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Text{.text = "Saved 2 minutes ago", .role = ui::TextRole::Caption, .style = app_styles::Card},
    ui::Button{.text = "Open", .style = app_styles::Card},
    // An explicit field beats the style's: 16 DIP margin, the minimum width kept.
    ui::Button{.text = "Close", .style = app_styles::Card, .margin = ui::Thickness{16.0f}},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Style{
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment
}
```

Plus the common fields `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### operator|=

```cpp
Style& operator|=(const Style& other)
```

Merges `other` into this style: `other` wins wherever it sets a field; unset fields pass through. Returns `*this`.

## class Spec

Any piece of UI: the one type-erased, move-only description value.

A [Spec](#class-spec) holds the already-built node of whatever spec (or hand-built [`unique_ptr<Element>`](element.md)) it was made from. It is what a component function returns, what a slot parameter takes, the type of every single-content field ([`.content`](#content), `.pane`, `.anchor`, ...) and of each entry in a [`.content`](#content) list, so the same value composes in all four places. It is consumed once. A default-constructed [Spec](#class-spec) is empty: a component that decided to show nothing, or a content field left unset. Containers skip an empty one.

Converts implicitly from any [SpecLike](#concept-speclike) value and from a `std::unique_ptr` to an [Element](element.md) subclass, which is what lets a braced list mix specs and hand-built controls.

A braced list of slots ([Grid](../layout/grid.md#uigrid) cells, [Canvas](../layout/canvas.md#uicanvas) items, tabs) is a `std::initializer_list`, which only hands out const references. [take()](#take) is const so the node can still be moved out of each slot. Each list drains its entries inside the full-expression that created it, so nothing reads a [Spec](#class-spec) after its node was moved out.

Handlers captured in a spec returned from a function must capture by value, or capture a reference to state that outlives the window; taking [`Property<T>&`](../core/property.md) parameters makes that the easy thing.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec user_row(ui::Property<std::string>& name, std::string email)
{
    return ui::HorizontalStack{
        .spacing  = 8,
        .content  = {
            ui::Icon{ .source = ui::glyphs::Contact, .accessibility = { .decorative = true } },
            ui::VerticalStack{ .content = {
                ui::Text{ .text = name },
                ui::Text{ .text = std::move(email), .role = ui::TextRole::Caption },
            }},
        },
    };
}

ui::Property<std::string> alice{"Alice"}, bob{"Bob"};
auto note = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Hand-built"); // a control made without a spec

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    user_row(alice, "alice@example.com"), // a component's result
    user_row(bob, "bob@example.com"),
    ui::Text{.text = "Sales"},            // a spec: built as the list is formed
    std::move(note),                      // an existing subtree: adopted unchanged
}});

bool show_footer = true;
ui::Spec footer = show_footer ? ui::Spec{ui::Text{.text = "Footer"}} : ui::Spec{};
```


## class SpecList

A built, owned list of elements. Move-only: it owns the built elements from the moment it is constructed.

The type of a container's [`.content`](#content) field. Written as a braced list in the common case, or as a single spec without braces when there is only one; build one up in a loop with [push_back()](#push_back), then move it into the field.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> names{"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"};
ui::SpecList rows;
for (const auto& name : names)
{
    rows.push_back(ui::CheckBox{.text = name});
}

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 4, .content = std::move(rows)});

// One element needs no braces.
ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 4, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Just this"}};
```

### nodes

```cpp
std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Element>> nodes
```

The built elements, in order. Public so a parent's [build()](#build) can drain it.


## class Control

```cpp
template <typename S> class Control
```

A typed, non-owning handle to the control a spec built.

`S` is the spec type; the control's type comes from the spec's `using control_type = ...;` line, so `ui::Control<ui::Button>` points at a [`ui::ButtonControl`](../controls/button.md#uibuttoncontrol). Declare one, hand it to the spec's `.control` field, and after the tree is built it reaches the live control. It changes no ownership: the tree owns the control, and the handle is empty until [build()](#build) has run, empty again once the control is destroyed (it watches the control). That includes a control built inside a subtree that was then thrown away, such as the children of a spec passed to a false [ui::when()](#when). Most controls need none; name only what you address later.

It is typed, so handing a `ui::Control<ui::TextBox>` to a [`ui::Button`](../controls/button.md#uibutton) is a compile error on that line. Where an API wants the control's pointer (`Element*`, `ButtonControl*`), the handle converts to it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Button> save;
ui::Control<ui::TextBox> name;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::TextBox{.placeholder_text = "Name", .control = name},
    ui::Button{.text = "Save", .on_click = [&] { save->set_text("Saved " + name->text()); }, .control = save},
}});

save->set_enabled(false); // the tree is built: the handles are live
```

### Type

```cpp
using ui::Control< S >::Type = typename S::control_type
```

The control class `S` builds.





## class ControlOut

```cpp
template <typename S> class ControlOut
```

The type of every spec's `.control` field: where [build()](#build) publishes the control it made.

It converts from a [`ui::Control<S>`](#class-control) handle, so a spec is written `.control = save`, and it only remembers where that handle is; the handle itself must outlive the build. App code never names this type: a component function that passes a handle on to the spec it returns takes a [`ui::Control<S>&`](#class-control), or a [`ui::Control<S>*`](#class-control) defaulted to `nullptr` when the handle is optional, and both convert. A custom spec declares its `.control` field as a [`ControlOut`](#class-controlout) of itself.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec save_button(ui::Property<bool>& dirty, ui::Control<ui::Button>* control = nullptr)
{
    return ui::Button{.text = "Save", .enabled = dirty, .control = control};
}

ui::Property<bool>      dirty{false};
ui::Control<ui::Button> save;
window.set_content(save_button(dirty, &save)); // `save` reaches the built button
```

### ControlOut

```cpp
ControlOut() = default
```

No handle: [build()](#build) publishes nothing.

### ControlOut

```cpp
ControlOut(Control<S>& handle)
```

Publish into `handle`.

### ControlOut

```cpp
ControlOut(Control<S>* handle)
```

Publish into `*handle`, or nowhere when it is null: for a handle that is only wanted sometimes (`.control = first ? &handle : nullptr`).

### publish

```cpp
template <typename C>
void publish(C* node) const
```

Stores `node` in the handle, if there is one. Called last in a spec's [build()](#build), through [ui::publish_control()](#publish_control).

## class LayoutSpec

How generated children are arranged: the type of every `.layout` field.

A layout is written as a plain value, [`.layout = ui::TileLayout{.min_row_spacing = 8}`](../controls/item-layouts.md#uitilelayout), with no `make_unique` and no setters. A name ending in [`Layout`](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout) is such a value and never a control: there is no `ui::Control<ui::TileLayout>`. An empty [LayoutSpec](#class-layoutspec) leaves the field's default in place, which for [ui::ForEach](../controls/for-each.md#uiforeach) is a vertical stack.

Which to reach for: hand-written children pick a layout control ([`ui::VerticalStack`](../layout/stack.md#uiverticalstack), [`ui::Grid`](../layout/grid.md#uigrid), [`ui::WrapPanel`](../layout/wrap-panel.md#uiwrappanel)); children generated from a collection pick a `.layout`.

A layout of your own is a class: derive from [ui::VirtualizingLayout](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-virtualizinglayout) or [ui::NonVirtualizingLayout](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-nonvirtualizinglayout) and hand a `std::make_unique<MyLayout>()` to the same field.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Photo
{
    std::string title;
};
ui::ObservableVector<Photo> photos;

window.set_content(ui::ForEach<Photo>{
    .items  = photos,
    .layout = ui::TileLayout{.min_item_width = 120.0f, .min_row_spacing = 8.0f, .min_column_spacing = 8.0f},
    .item   = [](const Photo& p) -> ui::Spec { return ui::Text{.text = p.title}; },
});
```

## class ControlLink

```cpp
template <typename S> class ControlLink
```

The type of a spec field that names another control by its handle: [InkToolbar](../controls/ink-toolbar.md#uiinktoolbar)'s `.target`, [TeachingTip](../controls/teaching-tip.md#uiteachingtip)'s `.target`, [RichText](../controls/rich-text.md#uirichtext)'s `.overflow`. Written `.target = canvas` with a `ui::Control<ui::InkCanvas>`, it links the two controls in either build order: at once when the target is already built, or as soon as the target's spec fills the handle. When the target is destroyed the control lets go of it, and a later build that fills the handle again links the new one. The handle must outlive the build, as for `.control`.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::InkCanvas> canvas;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::InkToolbar{.target = canvas}, // built first, linked once the canvas is built
    ui::InkCanvas{.height = 300, .control = canvas},
}});
```

### ControlLink

```cpp
ControlLink() = default
```

No link.

### ControlLink

```cpp
ControlLink(Control<S>& handle)
```

A link to the control `handle` holds or will hold.

### operator bool

```cpp
operator bool() const
```

True when a handle was given.

### resolve

```cpp
template <typename Fn>
void resolve(Element& owner, Fn link) const
```

For a spec's [build()](#build): calls `link(target)` now if the handle already holds a control, and again each time a build fills the handle, as long as `owner` lives. `owner` is the control being built, which keeps the target as an [ElementWatch](element-watch.md) (or unlinks itself in its destructor) so a destroyed target never leaves it holding a dangling pointer.

## class ElementLink

[ControlLink](#class-controllink) for a field that takes any control: [TeachingTip](../controls/teaching-tip.md#uiteachingtip)'s `.target` points at a button, a text box or anything else that has a handle. ## concept LayoutLike

```cpp
template <typename L> concept LayoutLike
```

Anything with an rvalue-qualified build() producing an owned Layout: what a `.layout` field takes. The four built-in layout values satisfy it, and so does an app's own.

## concept SpecLike

```cpp
template <typename S> concept SpecLike
```

Anything with an rvalue-qualified build() producing an owned Element. Because it is a concept, a mistake is reported at the caller's own line. Passing a non-spec into a child list gives "no conversion from 'int' to 'Spec'", not a template backtrace.

An app's own spec type satisfies it by providing [`std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> build() &&`](element.md), and then composes anywhere a built-in spec does.

Example: 
```cpp
struct LabeledField // a caller-defined spec
{
    std::string label;
    ui::Property<std::string>* value = nullptr;

    [[nodiscard]] std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> build() &&
    {
        return ui::build(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 4, .content = {
            ui::Text{.text = label},
            ui::TextBox{.text = ui::bind(*value)},
        }});
    }
};
static_assert(ui::SpecLike<LabeledField>);

ui::Property<std::string> name;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {LabeledField{"Name", &name}}});
```

## Aliases

### ItemTemplate

```cpp
using ui::ItemTemplate = Callback<Spec(std::size_t index)>
```

An item template in a spec: the [Spec](#class-spec) for item `index`, which may pick a different look by the item. Called only for the items a control creates rows for, and it may be called again for an item later, so it indexes into a model the caller keeps alive for the life of the control.

### SelectedItem

```cpp
using ui::SelectedItem = std::conditional_t<std::copy_constructible<T>, std::optional<T>, std::optional<std::size_t>>
```

What a typed view's `on_selection_changed` receives: a copy of the selected item (the first one when several are), or unset when nothing is selected. A copy is safe to keep. For an item type that cannot be copied it is the selected index instead.

## Functions

### operator|

```cpp
Style operator|(Style lhs, const Style& rhs)
```

Composes two styles into a new one; `rhs` wins wherever it sets a field. Usable in constant expressions: `constexpr Style s = styles::Spaced | styles::Leading;`.

### apply

```cpp
template <typename T, typename Fn>
void apply(Binding<T>& binding, Element& target, Fn sink)
    requires std::invocable<Fn&, const T&>
```

Seed a control property from a [Binding](../core/binding.md) and, if the binding is reactive, keep it in sync for as long as the node lives.

Together with [write_back()](#write_back), [shared_writer()](#shared_writer), [write_back_value()](#write_back_value), [apply_common()](#apply_common), [adopt()](#adopt), [ui::build()](#build) and [SpecList](#class-speclist), it is what the [build()](#build) of a spec for your own control calls. These helpers keep the same compatibility promise as [Element](element.md).

`sink` is called once immediately with the binding's initial value, then again on every change, through a [Subscription](../core/subscription.md) the target [Element](element.md) owns. That subscription dies with the node (see core/Property.hpp).

Example: 
```cpp
// A piece of a spec's build() && (see apply_common() for the whole shape):
std::unique_ptr<ui::TextControl> build_label(ui::Binding<std::string> text)
{
    auto node = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>();
    ui::apply(text, *node, [raw = node.get()](const std::string& v) { raw->set_text(v); });
    return node;
}
```

### write_back

```cpp
template <typename T, typename First, typename... Rest>
Callback<void(First, Rest...)> write_back(Binding<T>& binding, Callback<void(First, Rest...)> handler)
```

The change handler of an editable field: writes the control's new value back through a two-way binding, then runs the spec's own handler, unless the change came from a binding. Returns an empty callback when there is nothing to do.

So a spec's `on_*_changed` reports changes the user made. A value written into the bound property, or a change it causes, such as new items clearing a selection, updates the control and a two-way property without running the handler.

The first argument of the handler is the new value. Call it in [build()](#build) where the control's `on_*_changed` is installed, after [apply()](#apply) has seeded the value:

```cpp
void bind_value(ui::SliderControl& node, ui::Binding<double>& value, ui::Callback<void(double)> on_value_changed)
{
    ui::apply(value, node, [raw = &node](double v) { raw->set_value(v); });
    if (auto changed = ui::write_back(value, std::move(on_value_changed)))
    {
        node.on_value_changed(std::move(changed));
    }
}
```

### shared_writer

```cpp
template <typename T>
std::shared_ptr<typename Binding<T>::Write> shared_writer(Binding<T>& binding)
```

The writer of a two-way binding, shared between the handlers of an open/closed field, or null when the binding is one-way. See [write_back_value()](#write_back_value).

### write_back

```cpp
template <typename W, typename First, typename... Rest>
Callback<void(First, Rest...)> write_back(const std::shared_ptr<W>& writer, Callback<void(First, Rest...)> handler)
```

As [write_back()](#write_back), with a writer already taken by [shared_writer()](#shared_writer), for a field whose [apply()](#apply) sink also writes back what the control coerced the bound value to (a [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider)'s clamp), so the property ends up equal to the control without running the spec's handler:

```cpp
void bind_value(ui::SliderControl& node, ui::Binding<double>& value, ui::Callback<void(double)> on_value_changed)
{
    const auto write = ui::shared_writer(value);
    ui::apply(value, node, [raw = &node, write](const double& v) {
        raw->set_value(v);
        if (write && raw->value() != v) { (*write)(raw->value()); }
    });
    if (auto changed = ui::write_back(write, std::move(on_value_changed)))
    {
        node.on_value_changed(std::move(changed));
    }
}
```

### write_back_value

```cpp
template <typename T, typename... Args>
Callback<void(Args...)> write_back_value(const std::shared_ptr<typename Binding<T>::Write>& writer, std::type_identity_t<T> value, Callback<void(Args...)> handler)
```

As [write_back()](#write_back), for a field whose handler carries no value: an open/closed state, written as `value` when the handler runs (`.is_open` with `on_opened` and `on_closed`). Returns `handler` unchanged when `writer` is null.

```cpp
void bind_open(ui::PopupControl& node, ui::Binding<bool>& is_open, ui::Callback<void()> on_opened,
               ui::Callback<void()> on_closed)
{
    const auto open = ui::shared_writer(is_open);
    if (auto opened = ui::write_back_value<bool>(open, true, std::move(on_opened)))
    {
        node.on_opened(std::move(opened));
    }
    if (auto closed = ui::write_back_value<bool>(open, false, std::move(on_closed)))
    {
        node.on_closed(std::move(closed));
    }
}
```

### apply_common

```cpp
template <typename S>
void apply_common(S& spec, Element& target)
```

Apply the presentation and layout fields every spec carries.

Duck-typed on field names, so a spec of your own control works if it declares the common fields flat, with no shared base class.

The nine layout fields (margin, the six sizes, the two alignments) are bindable and optional. Precedence: a bound field always wins, a constant that is set wins, and `.style` fills in a field left unset. So `.style = styles::Spaced, .margin = Thickness{16}` gives 16, [`.style = styles::Spaced`](#spaced) alone gives 8, and `.width = size` follows `size` whatever the style says. A set value means what it says: `.width = 0` is zero wide, and only an unset width is Auto. A bound std::nullopt puts the control back to its own default (Auto, no limit, no margin, [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch)). Moves `spec.accessibility` out when it is not empty.

`.visible` maps to [Element::set_visibility()](element.md#set_visibility): false collapses the control, which then takes no room in layout, draws nothing, gets no input and leaves the tab ring. Nothing is destroyed, so a collapsed subtree keeps its state (typed text, scroll offsets, `.control` handles) and its bindings stay live. A spec without the field is always visible.

A caller-defined spec gets the whole common-field vocabulary by declaring the same fields and calling this from its [build()](#build).

Example: 
```cpp
struct Badge // a caller-defined spec
{
    ui::Binding<std::string> text{};

    ui::Style                                  style{};
    ui::Binding<std::optional<ui::Thickness>> margin{};
    ui::Binding<std::optional<float>>         width{}, height{}, min_width{}, min_height{};
    ui::Binding<std::optional<float>>         max_width{}, max_height{};
    ui::Binding<std::optional<ui::Alignment>> horizontal_alignment{}, vertical_alignment{};
    ui::Binding<bool>                         visible{true};
    ui::Accessibility                         accessibility{};

    using control_type = ui::TextControl;
    ui::ControlOut<Badge> control{};

    [[nodiscard]] std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> build() &&
    {
        auto node = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>();
        ui::apply(text, *node, [raw = node.get()](const std::string& v) { raw->set_text(v); });
        ui::apply_common(*this, *node);
        ui::publish_control(control, node.get());
        return node;
    }
};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {Badge{.text = "New", .style = ui::styles::Spaced}}});
```

### adopt

```cpp
Element* adopt(Element& parent, std::unique_ptr<Element>& node)
```

Adopt an owned child node into `parent`, wiring the parent link the same way every container's own add() does. Only sets the parent pointer: `node` keeps ownership, so the caller must store it in a member of `parent` that outlives the link. Returns the node as a non-owning observer, or nullptr when `node` is empty.

### publish_control

```cpp
template <typename S, typename C>
void publish_control(const ControlOut<S>& out, C* node)
```

Publish the built node through a spec's `.control` field, if a handle was given. Call it last in [build()](#build), after handlers are installed; see [apply_common()](#apply_common) for an example.

### content

```cpp
template <typename... S>
SpecList content(S&& ... specs)
    requires (std::constructible_from<Spec, S &&> && ...)
```

The variadic form of the brace list: builds each argument (a spec or a unique_ptr) into a [SpecList](#class-speclist), skipping empty ones. Useful where a list is passed through a function and braces would not deduce. To build a list in a loop, use [SpecList::push_back()](#push_back).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::SpecList actions = ui::content(ui::Button{.text = "OK"}, ui::Button{.text = "Cancel"});

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = std::move(actions)});
```

### when

```cpp
template <typename S>
Spec when(bool condition, S&& spec)
    requires std::constructible_from<Spec, S&&>
```

A spec that is only there when `condition` holds: `spec` when it is true, an empty [ui::Spec](#class-spec) (no element at all) when it is false.

A false condition skips the spec's own [build()](#build), but C++ evaluates the argument first: the children of a container spec (its [`.content`](#content) list) are already built by then, and are thrown away again. Their `.control` handles end up empty. Pass a callable returning the spec instead (the other overload) to build nothing at all when the condition is false.

The condition is read once, while the tree is built. For one that follows state, use the `.visible` field every spec has, [ui::Lazy](../controls/content-host.md#uilazy), or [ui::Match](../controls/content-host.md#uimatch).

Example: 
```cpp
bool is_admin = true;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Text{.text = "Report"},
    ui::when(is_admin, ui::Button{.text = "Delete all"}),
}});
```

### when

```cpp
template <typename F>
Spec when(bool condition, F&& make)
    requires std::invocable<F&&> && std::constructible_from<Spec, std::invoke_result_t<F&&>>
```

The lazy form of [ui::when()](#when): `make` is called only when `condition` holds, so a false condition builds nothing, children included. `make` returns a spec (or anything a [ui::Spec](#class-spec) is made from).

Example: 
```cpp
bool                    is_admin = true;
ui::Control<ui::Button> delete_all;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Text{.text = "Report"},
    ui::when(is_admin, [&] {
        return ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
            ui::Button{.text = "Delete all", .control = delete_all},
            ui::Button{.text = "Export"},
        }};
    }),
}});
```

### build

```cpp
template <SpecLike S>
std::unique_ptr<Element> build(S&& spec)
```

Builds a spec into an owned node, for handing a declared subtree to an imperative API that takes a unique_ptr.
